C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2.Summary: Open the findings window by proven payment, then flush the eight staged entries the window cannot otherwise hold. Two post-hoc historical rows land in live registry.xml — C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2 paying F172 and C-ARTIFACT-VALIDITY paying F39, each discharge witnessed by a present-tree artifact a reviewer can check without judgement — then a task runs scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire in the same execution wave, moving both rows and both findings to their retired siblings and stamping PaidBy. The move is this bundle's act, not a follow-on, because the flush deliverable needs the room the move opens and the close ceremony's post-archive move is structurally too late. Then the bundle flushes exactly the eight staged entries F196-F203 into findings.xml and decisions.xml, with the written base read back from newlineCount, never derived from a projection. F193 is re-derived from the code and on a fixture and does not hold in its strong form at this commit; the finding stays live and unpaid. Binding live rulings D28, D28.1, D30, D11; the record is this bundle's deliverable, so D30 is scoped, not skirted. Name re-searched at this commit: no archive directory, no live or retired registry row carries it.
C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2.Problem:
The staged buffer has outgrown the findings window. Eight entries, F196 through F203, wait in .ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md, and the live findings genre cannot absorb them: the persisted window is headroom="211" against a flush that lands at 245 lines — short by 34. The room comes from retirement, and retirement needs payers a derivation can read.
The population of unpaid payments is measured. At this commit there are 75 archive directories, 46 distinct registry row names across both layers, and 55 archived bundles with no row in either layer; their payments are invisible to derivePayerMap, so findings they settled can never become eligible. F172 is the worked example: the citation validator's qualifier-suffix slug grammar it describes was deleted by C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2's own work (commit 67bc55c, PR #74), and that bundle archived with no registry row at all, so F172 — live — cannot become eligible by any path. F39 is the same shape one bundle earlier: the lint honesty defect it describes was discharged by C-ARTIFACT-VALIDITY's shipped rule, and that bundle also has no row. derivePayerMap mints 54 payments at this commit; none names F21, F172, F193, or any of the eight staged entries.
The flush and the move must be ordered. Flushing before the move would write base = 7635 + 245 = 7880 against the persisted ceiling 7846 — ceiling-exceeded. The move must come first, open the window, and the flush consume it. The close ceremony's --retire happens after the archive git mv, which is after every task; a move that must precede a task cannot be the close's.
D30 freezes the record for a bundle that measures it. This bundle deliberately writes registry.xml, findings.xml, findings-retired.xml, registry-retired.xml, and decisions.xml — that is the deliverable, not an incidental measurement. The tension is stated here so it is not a silent D30 breach, and scoped in Constraints.

Goals.Goal:
Two post-hoc historical rows in live registry.xml, one per paying archived bundle, each payment proven before it is recorded. The payment set, each with the present-tree witness that discharges it:
C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2 pays F172. Witness: the finding's named mechanism is gone from the merged tree. grep -c expectedSlugFor and grep -c duplicateCount over src/ and scripts/ are each 0 at this commit; the removal lines are visible in git show 67bc55c -- scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts (PR #74, this bundle's own archived work); the validator's only remaining duplicate rule is duplicate-id over index ids at scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts:122, and the file carries 0 occurrences of "slug". The row's Charter names the symbols and the commit; a reviewer re-runs the greps.
C-ARTIFACT-VALIDITY pays F39. Witness: the shipped rules and the product behaviour. xml.comment-not-well-formed exists at src/lint/catalog.ts:529 with the named test "C-ARTIFACT-VALIDITY T-001 comment well-formed exact guide" at src/lint/catalog.test.ts:903; every artifact lint reads is parsed (readGraceXmlArtifact, src/artifact/xml.ts:201) and a malformed active artifact refuses with xml.parse and exit 1, with --explain xml.parse as the remedy (driven on a throwaway project at this commit); a plan comment containing two adjacent hyphen characters refuses with xml.comment-not-well-formed and exit 1 (same drive); and the archived plans the original count measured sit outside the scan set — the root lint exits 0 with the nine malformed archived XML files present and reports nothing about them. The "reports clean without checking" claim the finding names can no longer be produced: what the lint reports, it parsed.
Both payers are archived applied (spec and plan status="applied", measured), have no registry row in either sibling, and their specs do not mint the payment by prose: the payer-phrase sentences in C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2/spec.xml name only F161, and C-ARTIFACT-VALIDITY/spec.xml carries no payer phrase, so the row is the only route. One row's Pays may name several findings; here each row pays exactly one. status="live" on insert; the move rewrites it to "retired".

The move is a task's act, in the same execution wave as the row insert and the flush. After the two rows exist in live registry.xml, one bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire invocation stamps PaidBy, moves the two rows to registry-retired.xml (name equals an archive directory), moves F172 and F39 to findings-retired.xml, and flips the two matching RecordIndex Entry layer attributes. Validation then exits 0. The intermediate state between insert and move — finding-eligible-still-live and registry-eligible-still-live, twice each — is the D28.1 enforcement saying the move is due; it is a declared, verified working-tree state, never a commit validate:ci can see. No committed tree holds the intermediate occupancy.

The flush of exactly the eight staged entries F196-F203. Each entry becomes a Finding element in findings.xml (appended in anchor order after f193, the last live element) with a matching Entry line in decisions.xml. The buffer's entries are cut at the anchor that starts the next entry, dropping all trailing blanks; the buffer separates entries by anchors, not by delimiter lines. The body is copied verbatim; the heading line becomes the Title; the element adds three wrapper lines — the open tag, on its own line, and the close tag — with inline on the last prose line, so the landed element is the buffer span (heading plus body) plus three, a rule calibrated against the four entries the previous bundle flushed, which are in both the buffer and the record (f193 live: 31 prose lines to a 34-line element). The written root base comes from reading newlineCount back after the write, never from a projection; headroom is recomputed as ceiling minus the read-back base; the ceiling itself is untouched. A read-back base above the persisted ceiling stops the task and reports; it does not raise the ceiling. The projection (245 lines — 221 prose lines plus three wrapper lines per entry) is used only to check the ceiling is not breached; the staged buffer's stale copies of F192, F193, F194 and F195 — already in the record, three of them retired — are not re-flushed, and the flush selects by anchor id, never by position in the file.

F193 is re-derived and recorded; it stays live and unpaid. The shipped clamp (persistSnapshot in scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts) anchors its formula ceiling at the pre-move base: a genre that does not move gets ceiling = min(previousCeiling, preBase + H) and its window becomes min(previousWindow, H) — erased only where the window exceeded H. A genre that does move may grow its window to freed + H, one line per freed line, because the ceiling is re-anchored at the pre-move base. Fixture at this commit: a real retireRecord move touching findings and registry (moved = 2) left rulings.xml byte-identical at base="1697" headroom="186" ceiling="1883", the recomputed rulings H being 7 × 37 = 259, above the window. The finding's own table (370 to 245) describes the freed = 0 case, which is real; its strong narrative — the room survives only until the next --retire in any genre — does not reproduce at this commit. The flush order this bundle needs (move, then flush, nothing between them) is required by the arithmetic regardless, and the room the move opens is not erasable by an intervening unrelated-genre move at these numbers (re-clamp computes min(7846, 7635 + H) = 7846, H being the genre's 7 × median headroom of 245, a value distinct from the flush total that happens to equal it here). F193 is not paid: the clamp mechanism exists in the code, so paying it would retire live governance text on a false premise. The measurement is recorded here and in Assumptions; fixing or amending F193 belongs to a later bundle.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T1 (module-change shape): the record the retirement validator governs; no graph module is written, no src/ or scripts/ file is edited. Gates still run. Roadmap RM-GOVERNED-PATH. Binding live rulings: D28, D28.1, D30, D11. D27: nothing in this bundle is approved unread; the payment set is repaired by evidence, never by editing a finding to fit it. The payment set is exactly F172 and F39, named in Goals; no other token is paid by this bundle.

Payment evidence, the load-bearing rule, inherited from C-PAYMENT-RECORD and re-applied. Payments are proven first; the room is whatever falls out. Never select a payment because it frees the right number of lines. Sufficient, all of: (1) a present-tree witness — a symbol, a named test, or a file:line of the shipped behaviour that discharges the finding's defect, checkable by a reviewer without judgement; (2) the archived bundle that introduced that witness, with spec and plan status="applied"; (3) that bundle has no registry row in either sibling and its spec does not already mint the payment by prose, so the row is the only route; (4) the finding is still live. Insufficient, each refused: a bundle name or charter topic that merely sounds related; the finding's own discharge sentence without a tree check — a finding is never evidence of present state; sharing a file with a paid finding; a dated claim cited as present state. Candidates examined and refused for this bundle, with the check that refused them: F193 — the clamp mechanism exists (persistSnapshot); F190 — the indent drift reproduces on a fixture at this commit; F21 — the renamed mechanism exists (the finding itself records the rename); F185 — the named remedy never shipped (src/grace-context.test.ts carries zero explicit timeouts); F129 — the subject file exists (scripts/validate-walkthrough.ts; a content-only grep produces a false absence). If the provable payments did not open enough room, the bundle would say so and stop; they do.

Retire ownership: a task runs the move. The close ceremony's --retire is an authority act performed after the archive git mv; it cannot open room for this bundle because every task, including the flush, precedes the archive. An authority act between tasks is refused for the same reason F195 condemned the mutating test: a record operation with no acceptance criterion, no evidence trail, and writes outside any plan-declared scope is silent by construction, whoever performs it. A task performing the move deliberately — declared in the plan, scoped by its write scope, verified by pre-move eligibility findings and post-move validation green with re-derived roots — is the operator use C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2 explicitly preserved: do not add a validator-side refuse of production cwd, the operator command must still move the real record. The defect that bundle removed was a test performing the operation silently as an assertion side effect; this is the opposite shape: the operation is the deliverable, performed once, verified in both directions. Precedent: C-PAYMENT-RECORD's Goal — "--retire is this bundle's move, not a follow-on" — executed in one execution wave, identically here.

D30 scoped, not skirted. This bundle's purpose is to write the record: registry.xml (two historical rows), findings.xml and decisions.xml (the flush), and whatever the move writes — findings.xml, findings-retired.xml, registry-retired.xml, decisions.xml (Entry layer flips), and byte-identical rewrites of rulings.xml and rulings-retired.xml, which retireRecord writeFileSyncs on any successful move even when no decision is eligible. The freeze holds for the execution window that reads or rewrites the record files: no other dispatch touches the record while a record-writing task of this bundle is in flight, and no brief promises a frozen base across one. Findings raised while this bundle is open go to .ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md (F204 onward), never into the record under edit. No scalar count of a record file appears in any Constraint; occupancy and wrap figures live in Assumptions and expire. Ceilings are rewritten only by the move and never raised; a flush that would exceed a persisted ceiling stops and reports.

Order, ceiling, and CI. The committed sequence is: (1) the two historical rows in live registry.xml; (2) --retire in the same execution wave, before any commit validate:ci can see; (3) the flush of the eight staged entries, writing first and reading newlineCount back for the root base (F203's rule — a projection is never a written root attribute; the prior bundle's projection was one line high); (4) validation exits 0. Live registry occupancy after insert and before the move is the pre-insert live row count plus two, within the persisted registry ceiling (figures in Assumptions). A commit that holds the rows without the move is ineligible: validation reports registry-eligible-still-live and finding-eligible-still-live until the move runs. Do not raise the persisted ceiling. A second --retire after the flush is a byte-level no-op (moved = 0, early return before any write), verified on a fixture at this commit.

The 55-bundle audit is not this bundle. The rowless archived population at this commit is 55; this bundle records two payments because two payments are provable under the evidence rule above. With the corrected flush arithmetic, both are also required: the shortfall the flush must cover is 34 lines — 245 landed against the 211 window — F172's 29 freed lines do not cover it alone, and F39's 43 bring the total to 72. The selection ran the other way round: each payment was proven first, and the arithmetic is a consequence, not the criterion; had F39's witness not been provable, the flush would not fit and this bundle would say so and stop rather than stretch the payment set. The remaining rowless population is the later, larger audit charter; its boundary falls at the evidence rule, and the audit decides placement and population with its own proof standard. D11: nothing deferred here lacks a dependency or a conflict — the audit is a separate charter by design, and the refused candidates above stay live under their own tokens.
